the development of a novel approach to approximate dynamic programming that is both theoretically sound and computationally efficient.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose a new linear programming approach to approximate dynamic programming and provide theoretical and experimental results that demonstrate that the new approach can be competitive with the existing state-of-the-art.
we present a novel linear programming based approach to the approximation of the cost-to-go function of stochastic dynamic programming problems.
we present a new LP approach for ADP that can provide arbitrarily stronger guarantees than the state-of-the-art, while still being computationally efficient and scalable.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a seemingly small change in the formulation of an existing LP approach for ADP can lead to substantial improvements.
the use of linear programming for approximate dynamic programming can be significantly improved by relaxing the restriction to lower-bounding approximations.

the use of a lower bounding approximation in ADP is a choice rather than a requirement, and in some instances it is possible to relax this restriction in a way that is both computationally tractable and improves the approximation quality.
